create.name: Ramakrishna Vedanta Ashrama, Pittsburgh
create.bio:
Ramakrishna Vedanta Ashrama, Pittsburgh is a small centre in the Ramakrishna–Vivekananda tradition, housed in two neighbouring homes on Beatty Road in Monroeville, east of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Its shrine house was opened in September 2009 by Swami Swahananda, then head of the Vedanta Society of Southern California, who had encouraged local devotees to start an ashrama. It is run by its members, and monks and nuns of the Ramakrishna Order from centres across North America come through the year to teach.

The ashrama aims to make Vedanta practical as well as philosophical, in the light of Ramakrishna, Sarada Devi and Vivekananda, and to encourage service and respect between faiths. Programmes run in a hybrid format, in person and online: a Tuesday evening class on a scripture, currently the Uddhava Gita, discussion groups and meditation, weekend retreats and talks by visiting swamis, and festival pujas. A Sunday school for children under fifteen offers stories, chanting, meditation, music and art. Recordings of retreats and talks, including series on the Mandukya and Katha Upanishads, are posted on its website and YouTube channel, and members have also arranged talks at local universities.
